suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-33 adds this relationship only as a bounded chronic-anal-fissure continence association. A study of patients with chronic anal fissure found that mild fecal incontinence may be present at presentation rather than caused by internal sphincterotomy, so the diagnosis alone does not establish incontinence in every person or determine its cause. Require independently documented chronic anal fissure and fecal incontinence by validated assessment with compatible chronology, and colorectal review. Preserve prior sphincter injury or surgery, obstetric trauma, inflammatory bowel disease, pelvic-floor dysfunction, diarrhea, and other anorectal causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of chronic anal fissure and fecal incontinence by validated assessment

sourceReferences.citation: Elsebae MMA. A study of fecal incontinence in patients with chronic anal fissure: prospective, randomized, controlled trial of the extent of internal anal sphincter division during lateral sphincterotomy. World J Surg. 2007;31(10):2052-2057. PMID 17665247. doi:10.1007/s00268-007-9177-1.
sourceReferences.note: Study of fecal incontinence in patients with chronic anal fissure; the authors concluded that mild incontinence may be present at fissure presentation rather than result from internal sphincterotomy. Supports a bounded association and case-specific evaluation, not automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 17665247; study conclusion regarding mild fecal incontinence at chronic anal-fissure presentation

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Mild fecal incontinence may coexist with chronic anal fissure at presentation, but the study does not establish that anal fissure caused or aggravated incontinence in an individual without documented diagnoses, chronology, objective assessment, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this condition-specific association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Pain, sphincter spasm, and altered defecatory mechanics in chronic anal fissure may coexist with impaired continence, but the individual pathway must be established from anorectal examination, chronology, and objective sphincter evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Chronic anal fissure may coexist with mild fecal incontinence at presentation, but the evidence does not establish that fissure caused or aggravated incontinence in every individual; diagnoses, chronology, anorectal findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent diagnoses; baseline continence and chronology; objective anorectal and sphincter assessment; prior injury, surgery, obstetric, inflammatory, pelvic-floor, and diarrhea alternatives; colorectal review
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Prior anal-sphincter injury, obstetric trauma, or anorectal surgery
Inflammatory bowel disease, diarrhea, or other stool-consistency disorders
Pelvic-floor dysfunction, neurologic disease, or primary sphincter weakness
